documents.unit: University of Houston System, Information Security
documents.title: Usage of Artificial Intelligence at UHS
documents.stance_why: The page sets no stance on student or course AI use. Its only academic line, "Please check with the provost's office at your System university regarding specific use cases of AI tools in your curriculum", hands the decision elsewhere, so delegates.
documents.summary: System-level IT security guidance on AI tools, covering data classification limits, accuracy checks, and security controls for AI agents and self-hosted models. It sets no academic stance and sends academic questions to each System university provost. It says an official UHS AI policy is under development.

units.why: The preamble says UHS is "committed to ensuring that all constituents can use AI tools" "in a safe and responsible manner"; it states purpose and principle for the whole System, so P56 as a general informs statement.
units.anchor: committed to ensuring that all constituents can use AI tools

units.why: "this security and privacy guidance may evolve as circumstances change" says the guidance is provisional, so P54 (revisit the policy).
units.anchor: this security and privacy guidance may evolve as circumstances change
units.frag_end: develops further policy regarding the use of AI.

units.why: "UHS is developing an official AI policy" and readers are told to use these guidelines "during this process"; this makes the guidance interim. Nearest is P54 (provisional policy); it also tells readers where to send questions, which P54 does not capture.
units.anchor: UHS is developing an official AI policy.
units.frag_end: security@uh.edu should you have any questions, comments or concerns.
units.policy: UHS is developing an official AI policy; during this process, use these privacy and security guidelines or contact security@uh.edu with questions, comments or concerns.
units.fit_note: Also tells readers to use the interim guidelines and where to send questions.

units.why: "Do not use confidential, sensitive, or mission critical data (Level 1 data) or protected information (Level 2 data) with unapproved AI tools" is a ban on data inputs, so P50, must-not, restrict.
units.anchor: Do not use confidential, sensitive, or mission critical data

units.why: "You may use AI tools freely when using non-university or public information or creating new content" is a default permission for low-risk data. P02 fits partly because the permission is limited to public data.
units.anchor: You may use AI tools freely when using non-university or public information
units.frag_end: creating new content through the use of the tools.
units.fit_note: The permission is conditioned on the data being public or non-university, not an unconditional default.

units.why: "Sharing information with AI applications such as ChatGPT could cause data to be used by the tool for future use" explains the data risk (header "Avoid data sharing"), so P50, informs.
units.anchor: could cause data to be used by the tool for future use

units.why: "AI models can hallucinate ... or provide biased information, so it is critical that you verify any answers" tells users to verify output, so P31.
units.anchor: it is critical that you verify any answers an AI tool such as ChatGPT provides
units.frag_end: lack contemporary context to questions they answer.

units.why: "Consider how you share data with others ... could be used for AI training" advises caution with shared data; P50.
units.anchor: any information you make available to others or to the general public

units.why: "Please check with the provost's office at your System university regarding specific use cases of AI tools in your curriculum" hands academic-use decisions to each System university; no stance is set. P85 fits partly, since it is the provost office of each campus, not a school or department.
units.anchor: check with the provost's office at your System university regarding specific use cases
units.fit_note: Defers to each System university provost office rather than to colleges or departments; only academic line in the document.

units.why: "improving your AI literacy through online training such as courses on Linkedin Learning" recommends AI-literacy training, so P70.
units.anchor: improving your AI literacy through online training

units.why: "UHS faculty/staff can use Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with their UHS M365 account" names an institution-provided tool for faculty and staff, so P92.
units.anchor: UHS faculty/staff can use
units.policy: UHS faculty/staff can use Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with their UHS M365 account.

units.why: "Review your OneDrive/Sharepoint files to ensure that you are not oversharing" is advice to avoid exposing data; P50.
units.anchor: ensure that you are not oversharing

units.why: The sentence defines AI agents as "autonomous or semiautonomous software entities", setting the scope of the agent guidelines, so P61.
units.anchor: autonomous or semiautonomous software entities that utilize AI techniques
units.frag_end: in their digital or physical environments.

units.why: "Agents must use unique, non-human identities (service accounts) with dedicated credentials" with least-privilege and read-only defaults is a technical access-control rule for deployed agents; no type covers it (P07 is about student use of agents in coding work), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Agents must use unique, non-human identities (service accounts) with dedicated credentials
units.policy: Agents must use unique non-human identities with dedicated credentials, enforce least privilege, grant access only to required skills and resources, and default tool access to read-only.
units.uncovered_note: Security rules for identity, credentials and least-privilege access of AI agents that people develop or deploy.

units.why: "Require human-in-the-loop approval for high-risk actions" with "graduated autonomy based on risk" and defined agent scope limits what agents may do. It is not about decisions on people (P73), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Require human-in-the-loop approval for high-risk actions
units.policy: Define each agent's purpose and allowed operations, restrict it to its intended scope, apply graduated autonomy based on risk level, and require human-in-the-loop approval for high-risk actions.
units.uncovered_note: Limits on the scope and autonomy of deployed AI agents, with human approval for high-risk actions.

units.why: "Allow only approved tools for agent use" and "Review all third-party skills and extensions prior to enablement" require review and approval of AI tools before use, so P65.
units.anchor: Review all third-party skills and extensions prior to enablement.
units.policy: Allow only approved tools for agent use; review all third-party skills and extensions prior to enablement, because third party skills may include malware.

units.why: "all agent behavior must align with university acceptable use policies" requires compliance with existing university policy, so P77.
units.anchor: all agent behavior must align with university acceptable use policies

units.why: "Evaluate all integrations with external agents, APIs, and data sources" and "Ensure data sharing aligns with contractual and regulatory requirements" review third-party integrations and data sharing; P65.
units.anchor: Ensure data sharing aligns with contractual and regulatory requirements
units.policy: Evaluate all integrations with external agents, APIs and data sources, ensure data sharing aligns with contractual and regulatory requirements, and prevent unintended data exposure or exfiltration.

units.why: "Control and govern communication between agents" and prevent "privilege escalation through agent chaining" are architecture controls for multi-agent systems; no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Prevent unintended privilege escalation through agent chaining
units.policy: Control and govern communication between agents, prevent unintended privilege escalation through agent chaining, ensure combined workflows do not exceed intended authority, and design deployment architecture to enforce separation of duties.
units.uncovered_note: Architecture controls for multi-agent AI systems (communication, privilege escalation, separation of duties).

units.why: "Log all agent prompts, data access, and actions performed" and monitoring for anomalies is documentation and monitoring of deployed AI systems, so P98.
units.anchor: Log all agent prompts, data access, and actions performed
units.policy: Log all agent prompts, data access and actions performed, monitor agent activity for anomalies and potential threats, and use logs to support incident response and forensic analysis.

units.why: "Regularly review agent usage and business necessity" and "Decommission agents that are no longer required" set periodic re-evaluation of deployed AI; P98.
units.anchor: Regularly review agent usage and business necessity
units.policy: Regularly review agent usage and business necessity, decommission agents that are no longer required, periodically reassess access, tools and integrations, and keep agents aligned with current risk and governance standards.

units.why: "UHS faculty/staff can explore using Microsoft Copilot Agents" with enterprise data protection recommends an institution-provided tool to faculty and staff, so P92, encourage.
units.anchor: UHS faculty/staff can explore using Microsoft Copilot Agents
units.frag_end: data protection will protect the university's data.

units.why: "review any implementation with UHS Information Security" requires review before hosting a model locally; P65.
units.anchor: review any implementation with UHS Information Security
units.policy: If you host your own LLM, work with your local IT department or ISO and review any implementation with UHS Information Security.

units.why: The model must not be "prohibited via the TX DIR Prohibited Technology & Covered Applications list (i.e. Deepseek)" and must be verified by checksum; it limits which models may be hosted, so P65 with a fit note.
units.anchor: the model is not prohibited via the
units.policy: When hosting your own model, verify checksums or hashes prior to installing it and ensure it is not prohibited via the TX DIR Prohibited Technology & Covered Applications list.
units.fit_note: Also requires checksum verification of the model, which P65 does not name.

units.why: "Decide if real data has to be used or if synthetic data would be sufficient" advises minimizing real data in a hosted model, a data-protection rule, P50.
units.anchor: Decide if real data has to be used or if synthetic data would be sufficient

units.why: "If reusing the model for a different purpose, reset it back to the foundational model as residual training data may remain" is a hosting hygiene rule fitting no type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: reset it back to the foundational model
units.policy: If reusing a hosted model for a different purpose, reset it back to the foundational model, as residual training data may remain and may lead to unintended consequences.
units.uncovered_note: Advice to reset a self-hosted model to its foundational state before reuse to avoid leaking residual training data.

units.why: "If you are unsure whether you are using an AI application safely, please feel free to reach out" tells unsure users to ask the security office; P10 fits partly because the contact is the security office, not the instructor.
units.anchor: If you are unsure whether you are using an AI application safely
units.frag_end: reach out to us via security@uh.edu
units.fit_note: Directs users to the Information Security office rather than the instructor, and is about safe use of tools.

notes: Thin, security-focused System page; no teaching or learning rules. Navigation and resource link lists skipped. Several agent-security items are UNCOVERED (identity/least-privilege, scope and autonomy, multi-agent architecture, model reset).
